hints: Focus on the shape around the central atom, which is decided by how many bonding pairs and lone pairs surround it.
Notice that $\text{BF}_3$, $\text{CH}_3^+$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ all have three bonding regions and no lone pair on the central atom.
Consider what happens when nitrogen has three bonds plus one lone pair, and whether that lone pair lets the molecule stay flat.
walkthrough:
**Recall how planarity is decided**

Think VSEPR theory. A central atom with 3 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs is trigonal planar and flat. Adding a lone pair pushes the bonds out of the plane.

Rule to use:
$$\text{steric number} = \text{bonding pairs} + \text{lone pairs}$$

**Check the three flat species**

For $\text{BF}_3$, B has 3 bonds, 0 lone pairs, so trigonal planar. For $\text{CH}_3^+$, C has 3 bonds, 0 lone pairs (positive charge removed one electron), so trigonal planar. For $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$, each C has 3 bonding regions (including the double bond as one region) and 0 lone pairs, so each end is trigonal planar and the whole molecule is planar.

**Check ammonia**

For $\text{NH}_3$, N has 3 N-H bonds plus 1 lone pair. That is 4 electron pairs in total, tetrahedral electron geometry but pyramidal molecular shape.

Shape:
$$\text{3 bonding pairs + 1 lone pair = trigonal pyramidal}$$ 
A pyramid cannot be flat, so this is the species that is not planar.

options.A: Incorrect. In $\text{BF}_3$, boron has only 3 outer electrons to share, forming 3 bonding pairs and no lone pair. VSEPR gives trigonal planar with $120^{\circ}$ angles, so it is planar.
options.B: Incorrect. In $\text{CH}_3^+$, carbon would normally have 4 bonds, but loss of $\text{H}^-$ leaves 3 bonds and an empty p orbital with no lone pair. This is trigonal planar, just like $\text{BF}_3$, so it is planar.
options.C: Incorrect. In $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ (ethene), each carbon is $sp^2$ hybridised with trigonal planar geometry around it. The double bond prevents rotation, holding all 6 atoms in the same plane.
options.D: Correct. In $\text{NH}_3$, nitrogen has 5 outer electrons, forming 3 N-H bonds and keeping 1 lone pair. The lone pair repels the bonding pairs into a trigonal pyramidal shape, which is three dimensional and not planar.
